title: What links and browsers rely on

entities.title: The page's address
entities.summary: The forms of address that shared links and bookmarks use.
consumers: Links in documents, messages and READMEs that open a repository, a folder or a record
guarantees: The page is served at https://cyberspace-explorer.com/.
?url=<address> opens a repository: https://github.com/<owner>/<repository>, a GitLab project, either followed by /tree/<ref> and a folder.
#<folder> opens a folder; the repository root is the empty folder.
#<folder>|<kind>:<part ID or name> opens a part in that kind's drawing.
#<folder>|entity:<file name>#<record ID> scrolls to a record; without #<record ID>, to the file.

A last segment ~space or ~space:<scene> asks for the same place in Cyberspace: #<folder>[|<part, view or record>]|~space[:<scene>], where <scene> is tower (the default), city or street. Segments are encoded as the other forms encode them. #~waiting|~space is the root folder's tower. Where Cyberspace can't run, the place before the marker is shown flat; a page that predates the marker reads the folder and part the same way.
entities.compatibility: A new form may be added. A form that shared links already use keeps its meaning.

entities.title: Where tokens are kept
entities.summary: The storage key and shape that tokens readers have already saved are found under.
consumers: Readers' browsers that hold tokens saved by earlier versions of the page
guarantees: Tokens are kept under the key cyberspace-explorer.tokens, in sessionStorage (this tab) or localStorage (this browser).
The value is a JSON object from scope to token.
A scope is a host (github.com, or a GitLab's host), the host and an owner or group path, or the host and a repository path.
A token in sessionStorage wins over one in localStorage for the same scope.
entities.compatibility: The key keeps the page's earlier name, so tokens readers already saved are still found. Renaming it would silently drop every saved token.
